inputs.share_count_basis: Q2 2026 weighted-average shares for diluted EPS (479,824,000; Q2-2026 Financials line 57). Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows; buybacks (FY2025 $551M, H1 2026 $320M) are the mechanism that keeps it flat and are value-neutral here. No non-SBC issuance expected.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 MD&A adjusted-EBITDA reconciliation 'Share-based compensation expense' 163 (FY2024 37, FY2023 -14). Mostly cash-settled awards revalued to the share price, so the line is noisy and sometimes negative; no equity-award withholding taxes are reported (EquityAwardTaxes = 0 every period). Projected at 0.4% of revenue, the FY2019-FY2025 average (~$89M/yr on ~$27B), not the FY2025 spike.
inputs.fx_note: Statements are USD (IFRS, US-dollar presentation); NTR.TO quotes CAD on the TSX. Per-share values computed in USD and converted at USD/CAD 1.4254 (Yahoo USDCAD=X, 2026-10-10T04:21Z). Parity check: NYSE NTR USD 67.48 x 1.4254 = CAD 96.19 vs TSX NTR.TO CAD 96.33 at the same 2026-10-09 close -- a 0.15% tie that confirms rate, direction (USD->CAD multiply) and quote basis. refresh_price.py does not move fx_rate; re-check it on every refresh.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD-built rate. Cost of equity ~9.0% (US 10y ~4.3% + beta ~0.95 x 5.0% ERP); after-tax cost of debt ~4.2% (5.5% pre-tax, 24% tax); market weights ~76% equity (USD 32.4B market cap) / 24% net financial debt (USD 10.5B) -> 7.85%, rounded to 8.0%. Same WACC in every scenario: cyclicality and Jansen supply risk are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not as a discount-rate premium (charge risk once).
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost. The full IFRS-16 lease payment -- principal 419 + lease interest 65 = 484 in FY2025, 1.8% of revenue -- is deducted inside EBITDA via lease_cost_pct_path; lease liabilities (366 current + 974 non-current = 1,340 at 30-Jun-2026) are EXCLUDED from total_debt/net_debt. core_metrics total_debt of 12,728 includes those leases; the 11,388 used here is short-term debt 527 + long-term debt incl. current portion 10,861. D&A path excludes ~$420M/yr right-of-use depreciation so the lease is not charged twice in cash-tax EBIT. reported_fcf is likewise lease-consistent: OCF 4,007 - capex 2,005 - lease principal 419 = 1,583 (OCF - capex alone = 2,002; Nutrien's own FCF, which excludes investing capex, = 1,979).
inputs.nci_treatment: NCI is immaterial (FY2025 NI incl. NCI 2,297 vs attributable 2,267; NCI book equity 36 at 30-Jun-2026). Flows are consolidated; NCI deducted once at book in equity_bridge.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build, with the non-US/cyclical adaptations (USD flows vs CAD quote, IFRS-16 lease treatment B, NCI in the bridge). Nutrien is an operating company (crop-input retail + potash/nitrogen/phosphate production), so the SKILL.md routing table's cyclical-operating-company row applies; no bank/REIT/LIC features. First valuation of this ticker (no memory entry, no prior DCF). MID-CYCLE ANCHOR: adjusted EBITDA (company definition, pre-SBC) was 3,934 FY2018, 4,025 FY2019, ~3.5B FY2020, ~7.1B FY2021, 12,170 FY2022 (peak), 6,058 FY2023, 5,355 FY2024, 6,046 FY2025; H1 2026 3,535 vs 3,338 H1 2025. The Analysis JSON's 12.8B/4.9B/4.2B figures are UNADJUSTED EBITDA (incl. FY2023 $774M and FY2024 $530M impairments and FY2024 $360M FX loss; FY2025 includes a $301M Profertil gain) -- the adjusted series already strips those, which is why it is the anchor. Adjusted-EBITDA margins: 20.8% FY2023, 20.6% FY2024, 22.5% FY2025, 32.1% FY2022, 16.7-25.6% FY2019-21. The ebitda_margin_path is adjusted EBITDA LESS ~1pp of recurring cash costs Nutrien excludes from its adjusted figure (restructuring 47-68/yr, non-operating ARO/ERL spending up to 151/yr) -- cumulatively FY2022-25 OCF ran ~$1.9B below adjusted EBITDA - interest - tax. Base terminal 20.0% = ~21% adjusted, the FY2023-25 average; FY2022 peak excluded from every anchor; FY2018 not used (discontinued-ops gains, $1.8B New Brunswick impairment). CAPEX: FY2026 guide $1.95-2.05B (lowered in Aug-26) = ~7% of revenue, held ~7% -- sustaining + mine development ~1.6B plus modest investing capex, no supercycle. D&A guide $2.4-2.5B incl. ~$0.42B ROU depreciation -> 7.0% ex-ROU. CASH TAX: guided ETR on adjusted earnings 24-26%; FY2024-25 cash taxes (321/335) were depressed by the reversal of FY2022-23 over-payments (1,882/1,764), so cash tax ramps 22% -> 25%. WORKING CAPITAL: distributor/manufacturer, receivables + inventories exceed payables (~12% of revenue at year-end), so wc_capture is -10% of the revenue change. BUYBACKS: active repurchaser (FY2025 $551M, H1 2026 $320M, new 5% NCIB) -- the flat count is funded. STRATEGIC REVIEW of Phosphate (~6% of EBITDA), Trinidad nitrogen and Brazil Retail is ongoing with nothing signed: base case is the current consolidated entity; a sale is bull/bear framing only. BALANCE-SHEET SEASONALITY: net debt is taken at 30-Jun-2026 (latest) when receivables are seasonally high (8.7B vs 5.7B at Dec); Dec-2025 net financial debt was ~10.0B, so the June anchor is ~USD 0.9/share conservative.

equity_bridge.note: Total equity incl. NCI 25,938 less attributable 25,902, 30-Jun-2026 (Q2-2026 balance sheet)

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (5yr 2.5%, 3yr -0.6%) diverges by far more than 30% from revenue (5.2% / -10.8%) and EPS (41.9% / -31.0%). Every 3yr CAGR starts at the FY2022 peak and every 5yr CAGR at the FY2020 trough, so none is a usable growth rate; endpoint-driven noise in a deep cyclical. Book equity (flat ~$22-26B for seven years while ~$11B was returned via buybacks) is the steadiest signal and supports low-single-digit through-cycle growth.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF series = OCF - total capex - lease principal - SBC: FY2020 1,431, FY2022 5,268, FY2025 1,420. Owner-FCF CAGRs track reported (OCF - capex) CAGRs within ~3-6pp; SBC is small and noisy (cash-settled), so the gap is cycle timing, not SBC growth outrunning cash flow. FY2018 excluded as a base (discontinued-ops gains on SQM/APC/ICL stake sales, New Brunswick impairment).

base.narrative: FY2026 revenue ~+7.5% (H1 +8.5%, tight potash/nitrogen, record potash volumes 14.2-14.8Mt); FY2027 flat as Jansen Stage 1 ramps and the 2026 nitrogen tightness eases; then 2-3% (Retail structural growth + inflation). Margin fades from ~22% adjusted to the 21% FY2023-25 mid-cycle average (20% after recurring excluded costs) and holds there. Cap 15x terminal FCF (top of the 12-15x cyclical band: the terminal margin is already mid-cycle, so the cap only trims Gordon 18.6x, it does not re-charge the cycle).

bull.narrative: Demand absorbs Jansen: potash shipments keep growing 2-3%/yr on under-application in Brazil/SE Asia/India, El Nino supports crop prices, Retail compounds proprietary-product margins, and the Phosphate/Trinidad exits plus ~$200M cost savings lift the mix to a ~22.5% adjusted margin held through the decade.

bear.narrative: Jansen Stage 1 (4.15 Mtpa) plus Belarus/Russia volume push potash back toward the FY2024 trough by 2027-28; the 2026 nitrogen tightness reverses with gas spreads; Brazil Retail credit stress persists; Phosphate is sold at a trough price or retained at sub-par margins. Mid-cycle settles ~19% adjusted (18% net), below the FY2023-25 average, with Jansen Stage 2 capping any recovery.

scenario_narratives.base: Mid-cycle Nutrien: a tight 2026 (record potash volumes, firm urea) does not become the new base. Revenue grows ~7.5% in FY2026 and stalls in FY2027 as BHP Jansen Stage 1 ramps, then grows 2-3% with Retail. Margin settles at the FY2023-25 average adjusted EBITDA margin (~21%, 20% after restructuring/ARO cash costs the company excludes), capex at the lowered ~$2.0B guide, cash tax at the guided 24-26% ETR. The FY2022 peak and FY2024 trough are both outside the anchor.
scenario_narratives.bull: The Saskatchewan cost position plus the world's largest ag retailer compound: potash demand growth absorbs Jansen and FSU supply without a price reset, Retail proprietary products keep expanding margin, and portfolio optimization (Phosphate, Trinidad, Brazil Retail exits; ~$200M savings) concentrates capital in the highest-return assets. Adjusted margin ~22.5%, revenue growth 3-4% early.
scenario_narratives.bear: Jansen is the swing supplier the market fears: ~10% of global potash supply arriving low-cost from 2027 resets the potash price deck to the FY2024 level, nitrogen spreads compress as the 2026 disruption clears, US-China/US-Canada trade friction weighs on North American farm income and Brazil Retail credit stays tight. Revenue falls ~9% over FY2027-28 and margin bottoms at 17% (net), recovering only to 18%.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: a credible, well-funded low-cost entrant (Jansen, ~84% complete) arrives inside the forecast window and analyst views on potash pricing are split. Bull cut from 35% to 25%: it needs demand to absorb new supply AND the portfolio exits to land at good prices -- two independent things. Base 50% on the mid-cycle anchor.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value Nutrien on mid-cycle, not on the year in hand. Adjusted EBITDA has ranged 3.5B-12.2B since the merger; the base case capitalizes the FY2023-25 average margin (~21% adjusted) on lowered capex guidance, with leases charged once as operating cost and the Jansen supply wave priced as a 2027 stall in the base and a price reset in the bear. Risk sits in the flows and the 25/50/25 weights, never in the 8% USD WACC.
key_risks_to_valuation: BHP Jansen Stage 1 (4.15 Mtpa) and Stage 2 (~8.5 Mtpa total) reset long-run potash pricing below the mid-cycle anchor
Natural gas cost sensitivity (~$180M EBITDA per $1/MMBtu) and reversal of the 2026 nitrogen tightness
Phosphate/Trinidad/Brazil Retail strategic review outcomes and sale prices
Terminal multiple: the 15x cap (12x bear) binds below Gordon at 8%/2.5%, so value is sensitive to the cap chosen for a cyclical
USD/CAD: values are USD economics converted at a dated spot rate
